reading.body:
The lobbying around S. 2455 is dominated by music, media and copyright organizations, not by AI labs or data centers.

The bill's own text is tagged with two issues, copyright and likeness. The nineteen named organizations match that: record labels, publishers, collecting societies, a recording academy, a stage employees union, the Writers Guild, Getty Images, and the News Media Alliance. AT&T appears twice as a filer, and one AI company, Bria Artificial Intelligence, appears once. The rest of the field is the rights-holder side of the content economy.

This matters for AI because the fight over training data and generated likeness is being fought by the parties who own the catalogs, not by the parties who build the models. The bill carries four cosponsors across both parties, Welch and Schiff for the Democrats, Blackburn and Hawley for the Republicans, which suggests the copyright and likeness framing has bipartisan purchase. A filing that names a bill shows the bill was an issue in the lobbying, not the position taken on it, so nothing here says which side any organization argued for.

What the data does not cover is decisive. It gives no vote counts, no committee action, no text of amendments, and no spending figures. It records that 35 filings for 2025 or later name the bill, and it lists the organizations behind them, but it cannot show whether that pressure changed the bill or whether the bill is moving at all. The status date is 2025-07-24, and nothing here indicates what happened after it.

summary: S. 2455, TRAIN Act Transparency and Responsibility for Artificial Intelligence Networks Act. Latest status date 2025-07-24. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: copyright and likeness. 35 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
